title: India's first rocket parts arrived at the launch site by bicycle and bullock cart. November 21, 2026.
excerpt: The birth of India's space program at Thumba, a record month for Coal India, and the ex-ISRO engineer who now points satellites at crop fields instead.
bodyHtml:
India's first rocket parts arrived at the launch site by bicycle and bullock cart

On November 21, 1963, India launched its first sounding rocket from Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. The US-supplied Nike-Apache rocket carried a French payload, and a local church, St. Mary Magdalene, was converted into an early assembly facility and control room. Vikram Sarabhai and a young Abdul Kalam were both central to the launch - and that one rocket became the starting point for ISRO, growing into the infrastructure base for India's entire space program.

India's coal supply just hit an all-time monthly high

Coal India supplied 70.3 million tonnes of coal in October 2026 - its highest-ever monthly supply, beating the previous record of 69.4 million tonnes set just seven months earlier in March 2026. Production also hit a record: 67.2 million tonnes, up 19% year-on-year. Supply to the power sector alone reached an all-time monthly high of 57.1 million tonnes, keeping the grid running through peak demand.

He left ISRO to point satellites at Indian farms instead

Prateep Basu spent years building satellites for ISRO before co-founding SatSure in Bengaluru in 2017, using satellite data to help banks, insurers, and governments make decisions about agriculture, infrastructure, and disaster response. SatSure just raised Rs 60 crore from a government-backed space fund, valuing the company at roughly Rs 870 crore, with private banks also lining up to invest in what satellite data can tell them about risk on the ground.

Three stories today, all pointed at the same instinct: start with what you have, and build toward the gap that's actually there.

coverHeadlines: Coal still powers most of India's grid. Last month, Coal India moved more of it in a single month than ever before.
India's first rocket parts arrived at the launch site by bicycle and bullock cart.
Prateep Basu spent years building satellites for ISRO. Then he started a company to point them at crop fields and flood zones instead.
